kicker: Matsue · Izumo Taisha · Iwami Ginzan — Oct 20–23, 2026
title: Shimane
dek: Four days on Japan's least-touristed coast: a UNESCO silver-mine town reached by a six-seat cart with no reservations, the shrine where the old calendar says all of Japan's gods are somewhere else this October, and the country's best lake-clam broth.
footer: Location photos via Wikimedia Commons — tap any credit for its source, author and license.
intro: Matsue base for the castle and Izumo Taisha, then a one-way relocation with luggage to Oda/Omori for the Iwami Ginzan silver mine before looping back east to fly out of Izumo. Built for a party of 8, two with limited walking tolerance, no rental car.
verified: ⚠ Draft — Pass A (canonical/official-source) research only, 2026-08-28. Matsue Castle, Izumo Taisha, and the Iwami Ginzan transport chain (JR + Iwami Kotsu bus + Ginzan Cart) confirmed against official/operator pages. Entry/visa and the US travel advisory could NOT be confirmed this pass — both official sources (mofa.go.jp, travel.state.gov) returned HTTP 403 to a non-browser fetch; needs a networked/browser recheck before publish. Re-check before travel: Ginzan Cart operating days/hours (weather-dependent, can suspend without notice), all bus/train timetables (rural lines revise seasonally), Matsue Castle's post-Jul-2026 pricing, and the Izumo Taisha Kamiari-zuki dates for any later trip (2026's fall in Nov, not October).

items.note: outside Matsue/Izumo station areas, English drops off fast — expect to point and show text

items.native: 食物アレルギーがあります
items.note: follow with the specific allergen; staff will often bring a written ingredient list

items.native: 私はベジタリアンです
items.note: dashi (fish stock) is in almost everything, including soba broth — ask specifically

items.native: 救急車を呼んでください
items.note: dial 119 directly if you can; English-speaking interpreters are patched in on both 110 and 119

items.native: 警察を呼んでください
お手洗いはどこですか？

items.note: useful at the Ginzan Cart queue — a first-come, first-served 6-seat shuttle

items.romanization: Hachinin desu ga, seki wa arimasu ka?
items.note: call ahead — small soba houses here often can't seat a walk-in group of 8 without warning

items.situation: Can I pay by IC card (ICOCA/Suica)?
items.native: ICOCA（交通系ICカード）は使えますか？
items.romanization: ICOCA (kōtsūkei IC kādo) wa tsukaemasu ka?
items.note: the answer is no once you're west of Izumo-shi Station — carry cash for Oda/Omori

items.situation: Where is the bus stop / bus to Omori?
items.native: 大森行きのバス乗り場はどこですか？
items.romanization: Ōmori-yuki no basu noriba wa doko desu ka?

items.situation: Is there a step-free / elevator route?
items.native: エレベーターはありますか？
items.note: rural stations and heritage buildings often don't have one — worth confirming before committing to a route

items.native: どうもありがとうございます
